title: Document-Based Questioning and Recording Evidence
summary: How to use board papers, policies, minutes and data to question interviewees effectively, and how to record interview evidence so it is accurate, complete and usable later.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: How to use board papers, policies, minutes and data to question interviewees effectively, and how to record interview evidence so it is accurate, complete and usable later.
Learning Objectives: Use documents to test accounts and confront inconsistencies
Record interview evidence accurately and contemporaneously
Assess when an interview record must meet a higher evidential standard
Syllabus: Selecting and sequencing documents for disclosure in the interview
Putting inconsistencies to the interviewee fairly
Note-taking, recordings, transcripts and agreed notes
Storing, sharing and relying on interview records
Intended Audience: Supervisors and inspectors who conduct on-site visits, thematic reviews and governance assessments
Staff assessing fitness and propriety of directors and senior managers, including authorisation teams
Team leaders who plan inspections and review interview evidence before findings are issued
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of on-site inspections or firm engagement is helpful. No prior interview training is required.
Core Reading: Rebecca Milne and Ray Bull, Investigative Interviewing: Psychology and Practice (1999)
IMF, The Making of Good Supervision: Learning to Say "No" (Staff Position Note SPN/10/08, 2010)
Daniel Kahneman, Thinking, Fast and Slow (2011)
